notes: Access: robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (confirmed by prior Home-Decor pass and re-checked); curl_cffi impersonate=safari17_2_ios was the only working HTTP profile (matches prior pass finding). Fetched https://www.meesho.com/ and captured the SSR __NEXT_DATA__ payload containing the site's full navUrls list (362 url/title pairs, matching the prior pass's '363-entry navUrls list' count). Scoped review strictly to the 4 Home & Kitchen sub-menus per this company's department-scoped name (Home Decor, Kitchenware, Home Textiles, Home Essentials) as the prior pass documented them. Searched the full nav list (all departments, not just Home & Kitchen) case-insensitively for bestseller/best-seller/best seller/top-seller/trending/popular wording: the ONLY hits are /toys-best-sellers/pl/66zg 'Best Sellers' (Toys department) and /trending-lehengas/pl/6lqb 'Trending Lehengas' (Fashion department) -- both out of Home & Kitchen scope. Zero Home & Kitchen-scoped Bestsellers-type nav entry exists. Separately probed 6 common Bestsellers-shaped URL guesses directly (/best-sellers, /bestsellers, /best-selling-products, /top-sellers, /trending, /trending-products): all returned HTTP 200 with ~48.43-48.44KB bodies containing __NEXT_DATA__/clpListing placeholders identical in structure and near-identical in byte length to a deliberately nonexistent control URL (/nonexistent-random-xyz-123 -> 48449 bytes) -- this confirms Meesho serves a generic client-side SPA shell for any unmatched path (a soft-404), not real PLPs, at every one of these guesses. sitemap.xml is a sitemap-index of PDP-only sub-sitemaps (product detail pages), no category/PLP-level sitemap exists to cross-check. Site's own search (/*/search) and facet/count APIs (/*/facet_clp/*) are robots.txt-disallowed (confirmed by prior pass), so site search could not be used as supporting evidence -- not needed here since nav+URL evidence is already conclusive. Mid-session the host began returning 403 Access Denied (Akamai) on both a previously-working category PLP (dinnerware) and the homepage itself; stopped further requests to this host per the first-block rule rather than escalating to Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome to route around an explicit block. This prevented checking individual Home & Kitchen category PLPs' on-page sort widgets (e.g. a 'Popularity' sort order) and rendered footer links, but neither would qualify as a genuine Bestsellers PLP under this brief's rules even if present (a sort order is an arbitrary filter, not a named merchandising category), and the footer's own SSR node was already observed empty ({}, client-hydrated) in the captured payload before the block. Conclusion: no genuine Bestsellers/Best Selling/Top Sellers/Trending/Popular Products PLP exists within Meesho's Home & Kitchen scope.
